errors.evidence: Thought: Based on the information, I’ve reasoned out the following scenario. The compound meeting the criteria (molecular weight ≤100 g/mol, exactly 6 heavy atoms, ≤1 hydrogen bond acceptor, and a complexity between 10 and 15) is found in the NCATS Food Additive Status classification within PubChem. Its record shows that it has two possible enzyme transformation annotations. Analysis of the gene–chemical co-occurrence data (i.e. the list of chemicals that occur with genes in both enzyme transformation records) reveals that among the shared co‐occurring compounds the heaviest by molecular weight is the one that corresponds to benzoic acid. Benzoic acid (a common metabolic derivative from aromatic compounds) has a higher molecular weight (approximately 122 g/mol) than the alternative co‐occurrence compound (for example, the hydroxylated product phenol, which is ≈94 g/mol). PubChem shows that benzoic acid is indexed with CID 180.
